label: end-of-episode timer (last ~8-10 trials)
explanation: Update-gate unit that is completely silent for the first ~80 trials of an episode and turns on only near the end: 0 activations before trial 79, 5.5% rate on trials 80-89, 47.5% on trials 90-99, which hold 95% of the activation mass. Activation ramps up over the final trials, so the strongest activations come from the very last trials. The unit also tracks the value head: 95% of the mass is in the lowest value bin (value < 5.22, where expected remaining return shrinks), and none of it is at value >= 7.13. Phase modulates it inside the late window: D2 is strongest (55% of mass), D1 next, GO weakest. Within a trial it tends to rise from GO to D2, and it peaks at D1 after an unrewarded trial (r0) or at D2 after a rare transition. Choice, state, transition, reward, stay/switch and the good state barely matter (lift near 1x). On dev, ep_trial >= 92 scores P 0.55, R 0.79, F1 0.65, mass recall 0.88. ep_trial >= 90 scores mass recall 0.95 but P 0.48. Adding a phase condition (no GO before trial 95) only reaches F1 0.68. Precision is limited because inside the window the unit is graded and does not fire on every late step: it often skips early-trial GO steps and rewarded D1 steps. This reads as an internal clock or value-decay signal whose magnitude carries time-to-end. The episode position is not a direct input, but the agent can infer it from elapsed time, so the predicate is not FUTURE.
